# Quran Tajweed Benchmark

A test for systems that listen to Quran recitation. Two questions: does the system leave correct recitation alone,
and does it catch the mistakes? Quran Lab runs every system on the leaderboard itself, on the same audio.

**Leaderboard:** [Quran Tajweed Leaderboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Quran-Lab/quranic-asr-leaderboard)

## What is public, and what is not

- **Public, here: correct recitation.** 3,910 recordings, 9.2 hours, each with the mushaf text, the
  phonemes and every legal way of reading its ayah. Most are by 22 professional reciters whose recordings
  were held out of training.
- **Private: the recitations with mistakes.** The leaderboard also scores every system on recordings with one
  known mistake, in the studio and through a phone. Those recordings are not published, so that nobody can train
  on them. Send a model and Quran Lab runs it on them (see below).

## Configs

All audio is 16 kHz mono FLAC. Every config has a single split, `test`.

| config | recordings | hours | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `correct_t1p_dev` | 930 | 2.20 | Held-out panel, development half: 6 professional reciters. Use it to tune. |
| `correct_t1p_test` | 1,780 | 4.24 | Held-out panel, test half: 16 professional reciters. The leaderboard's correct-recitation numbers are measured on these recordings. |
| `correct_t1` | 153 | 0.34 | An older held-out reciter (Ali Hussein Qasim). |
| `correct_t1x` | 1,044 | 2.37 | 4 reciters whose voices are in Quran Lab's own training mix, marked so: held out for other models, not for ours. |
| `correct_t1w_test` | 3 | 0.03 | Women: published competition recordings held out of every training pool (2 reciters, 3 recordings: all that passed

# Quran tajweed pilot: Iqlab (professional reciters)

Pilot dataset for Qur'anic recitation assessment (MSc project): ayah-level recordings by professional
reciters, with Uthmani text and reference phonemes. **Text and reference phonemes are machine-generated
and not yet verified by a Tajweed expert.**

## Columns
- `id`: `<speaker_id>_<SSSAAA>`
- `tajweed_target`: rule the ayah was selected for (here `iqlab`)
- `surah`, `ayah`: location
- `speaker_id`: reciter
- `audio`: 16 kHz mono recitation of the ayah
- `ayah_uthmani`: Uthmani text of the ayah
- `phoneme_ref`: reference phonemes (Hafs, ayah-by-ayah with a stop at the ayah end, closed-lip `m̃` for
  Iqlab), from Quranic Phonemizer 3.0.5
- `phoneme_realized`: empty. Recitations were not annotated; they are assumed correct.
- `duration_s`, `source_url`: provenance

## Reciters and sources
Audio comes from [EveryAyah](https://everyayah.com), which hosts recitations by their reciters:
Mishary Alafasy (`alafasy`), Mahmoud Khalil Al-Husary (`husary`), Mohamed Siddiq Al-Minshawi, Murattal
(`minshawy`) and Ali Al-Hudhaify (`hudhaify`). Each row's `source_url` points to the original file.
Reference phonemes: [Quranic Phonemizer](https://pypi.org/project/quranic-phonemizer/) (MIT).
